newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish unions warn of threat to national pay accord.
newsitem.headline: Irish unions warn of threat to national pay accord.

text.p: The Irish Congress of Trade Union (ICTU) said it would meet the government and employers later on Wednesday to warn them of the threat to Partnership 2000 caused by the failure to implement key elements of the agreement.

Partnership 2000, agreed by government, unions and employers earlier this year, provided for wage rises of 9.25 percent over a three-year period and promised tax reductions of one billion punts over the life of the accord.

It was the fourth agreement of its type. Centralised pay accords have been credited with making a strong contribution to Ireland's high rates of economic growth in recent years by helping to keep a lid on wage inflation and industrial unrest.

"Government and employers would be making a grave mistake if they take for granted the good industrial relations climate which has made a vital contribution to our economic progress in recent years," ICTU general secretary, Peter Cassells, said in a statement.

"Failure to implement the non-pay elements of Partnership 2000 or to honour the spirit of the partnership which underpins the agreement would threaten the future of partnership and the stability of the current agreement," he said.

ICTU said little or no progress had been made in implementing key commitments in Partnership 2000 such as the establishment of a National Centre for Partnership which would have a key role in promoting partnership in the workplace.

ICTU also said it was extremely short-sighted to use the recent pay settlement with Ireland's nurses as a straight jacket to deny fair play to other health carers instead of using the commitment by unions in Partnership 2000 to improving the quality of public service as the basis for developing a top class health service.
The resolution of a recent nurses' dispute over pay and conditions has triggered further disputes within the health services industry with Irish ambulancemen currently threatening strike action.

Ireland's largest union, SIPTU, on Wednesday called on Irish health minister Michael Noonan, to intervene to avert serious disruption if Monday's strike by 600 members of the emergency ambulance service takes place.
